explanation: Domain is every x the function will accept; range is every y it can produce. For a square-root graph the curve cannot start until x reaches h (you can't take the root of a negative), so the orange bracket on the x-axis opens at h. The lowest the curve ever gets is its starting height k, so the violet bracket on the y-axis opens at k. Slide h and k and watch both brackets and the interval readout slide with the corner.
bullets: Domain reads along the x-axis; range reads along the y-axis.
[ means the endpoint is INCLUDED; +inf always gets a round ) (never reached).
The corner point (h, k) is exactly where both intervals begin.
